promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Don't make up the missed miles. Heat, 5.5 hours of sleep and work stress cost you last week, so next week holds near 29 miles with one trimmed quality session and a 10-mile long run.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer:
No, don't make up the miles. You ran about 9 miles under the plan, but the cause was heat, 5.5 hours of sleep and work stress, not lost fitness.

Adding those miles back would stack extra load on a body that is already running hot. One light week costs you very little, and next week goes back up to about 29 miles.

new.analysis:
Last week was limited by heat, sleep and stress, not by fitness. Your easy runs went from 9:50/mi at 138 bpm to 10:28/mi at 151 bpm, so heart rate rose 13 beats at a slower pace. That is what hot early starts and short sleep do to heart rate, and the four weeks before it show the fitness is there.

| Day | Planned | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue Aug 25 | 6 mi easy | Ran 6.0 mi, heart rate 153 |
| Wed Aug 26 | 8 mi with 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00 | Ran 6.0 mi, 2 reps at 8:18, stopped |
| Thu Aug 27 | 5 mi easy | Missed |
| Sat Aug 29 | 4 mi easy | Ran 4.0 mi |
| Sun Aug 30 | 13 mi easy, heart rate under 150 | Ran 11.0 mi, heart rate 156, two water stops |

Stopping the threshold session and cutting the long run were sensible calls. With the heart rate that high, finishing them would have bought more fatigue than fitness. Skipping Thursday cost you little for the same reason.

Only 10.8% of your running time was in zones 1 and 2, because heart rate sat in zone 3 on almost every run. That was the heat, not a training mistake. It is why the limit this week is heart rate and not pace.

For next week I am holding volume near 29 miles, a little above the 27 you ran and below the 32 to 35 of early August. The week keeps one quality session, trimmed to 20 minutes of threshold work, because hard running in heat cost more than it gave. The long run steps back to 10 miles so you can finish it at a controlled heart rate.

You are 8 weeks out from the race, which leaves enough time. A 3:45 needs about 8:35/mi, and the long run is the session that matters most. Once sleep and heat ease, I want it back to 12 miles, then longer, with marathon-pace segments and a medium-long run during the week. If sleep stays short, I will slow that climb instead of forcing it.

Sleeping better will do more for you right now than any session. If you can sleep somewhere cooler for a few nights, or run first thing and get to bed early, do that.

settingsProposalBullets: Your apartment is hot and the AC is out until about this week, so short sleep is likely for a few more days.
Your easy runs usually sit around 138 to 140 bpm, so I would cap easy heart rate at 145 and long runs at 150.
Marathon pace for 3:45 is about 8:35/mi, and your threshold pace is about 8:00/mi in cool weather.
Your right knee had outside tightness in mid-August that settled by Aug 23, and hip and glute work stays in your week.

safetyCallouts.title: Keep an eye on the tiredness.
safetyCallouts.body: Heat, short sleep and work stress can explain feeling drained, which is why the plan stays light. If you still feel flat after a week of normal sleep, or you ever feel dizzy or faint on a run, stop and see a doctor.
